claims.content: The Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A Customer with won auction items proceeds through checkout by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type, thereby completing the transaction.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer has won auction items and begins checkout with the intent to pay for them.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer has chosen which won items to pay for, selected a shipping method, and selected a payment type, completing checkout/payment for those items.
in_scope_actions: choosing which won auction items to pay for
excluded_adjacent_actions: placing bids or participating in auctions
post-payment fulfillment, physical shipping, or delivery execution
external payment processing/authorization beyond selecting a payment type
variant_dimensions: the set of won items selected for payment

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has at least one unpaid won auction item for which checkout/payment has not yet been completed.
The Customer has previously chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default method of payment.
The Customer's account status (e.g., having won items) is a condition that must hold before successful checkout.

missing_aspects: Evidence implies account status is a condition but does not explicitly state that the account must not be in 'locked' or 'review' status to proceed.

claims.content: The Customer clicks a payment initiation link/button—such as the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email, the Winnings Alert link, or a 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button—to start checkout and payment.
The Customer chooses which won auction items to pay for from a list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking one of three buttons: 'Check out with PayPal', 'Check out with Amazon', or 'Checkout Later'.
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.

Diverges from Step 4: Rather than selecting a checkout option, a returning Customer whose default Method of Payment is PayPal or Amazon Payments is routed to a specific page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for their winnings.

Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may select PayPal as the payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section, instead of using credit card or Amazon Payments.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may choose to pay using Amazon Payments, which opens a new browser session to register or log in, if they have purchased from Amazon in the past.

Diverges from Step 5: If PayPal is the Customer's default Method of Payment, the system sends an email notification upon winning an auction and the Customer must manually log into their JTV account to process payment within 7 days.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may complete payment by logging in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page, rather than creating a new account or using Amazon.

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering Country (defaulted to United States), and choosing a payment method: either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card'.

Diverges from Step 4: If the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button or radio button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a DIV layer with specific text stating that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the window expires.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer does not complete payment for the won item(s) within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, the system cancels the unpaid order(s) and places the item(s) into 'Hold' status. Exit: the use case terminates without payment; the order(s) are cancelled.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer fails to complete the payment transaction within seven days (168 hours) of the auction's closing date/time, the email will include a notification that the Customer's account may be suspended.

Diverges from Step 5: If a PayPal or Amazon Payments Customer's unpaid order(s) are more than 7 days old (expired/unresolved auction winnings), the system automatically locks the Customer's account and puts it into 'Review Status'; because the order(s) are already cancelled, the Customer cannot unlock the account by paying for them. Exit: the use case terminates without payment; the account is in Review Status and cannot be unlocked by the Customer's payment.

missing_aspects: Explicit exit condition for the use case (e.g., termination vs. suspension)
Confirmation that the order remains payable until the deadline
Evidence that the use case terminates upon this potential suspension
Evidence distinguishing this as a definitive outcome rather than just an email notification

claims.content: The 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid' for items where the transaction has been successfully completed.

After the Customer completes the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.

quality_flags.detail: [trigger_preconditions_coverage] Preconditions include only a vague claim that account status must hold, but do not explicitly require the Customer's account to be unlocked/in good standing before the Customer can initiate checkout from the payment link/button. If a locked/review account cannot initiate payment, this required state is missing. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that checkout/payment initiation is blocked for locked/Review Status accounts; cited evidence supports successful checkout completion and restrictions on bidding/payment, not initiation.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 (0-based index 2) reports only an email notification that the Customer's account may be suspended and gives no explicit outcome (terminate, return, handoff, or terminal failure), so the branch lacks clear exit coverage. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that the account-suspension notification is sent by email; the cited cards support account suspension, not the email medium.; Explicit recovery/exit evidence; the cited cards do not state that the use case terminates without payment, only the cancellation/'Hold' outcome.; Explicit evidence that cancellation/'Hold' status applies to all unpaid orders, not only Amazon/PayPal orders.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Main Flow step 5 only gets the Customer started on the external payment process; it does not complete the Amazon/PayPal checkout, process a successful transaction, or return the Customer to a Thank You page. Therefore the postconditions ('Payment Status = Paid' and 'Customer returned to Thank You page') are not reachable from the Main Flow as written. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Main Flow step 5 only gets the Customer started on the external payment process; it does not complete the Amazon/PayPal checkout, process a successful transaction, or return the Customer to a Thank You page. Therefore the postconditions ('Payment Status = Paid' and 'Customer returned to Thank You page') are not reachable from the Main Flow as written.

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] Preconditions include only a vague claim that account status must hold, but do not explicitly require the Customer's account to be unlocked/in good standing before the Customer can initiate checkout from the payment link/button. If a locked/review account cannot initiate payment, this required state is missing.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 (0-based index 2) reports only an email notification that the Customer's account may be suspended and gives no explicit outcome (terminate, return, handoff, or terminal failure), so the branch lacks clear exit coverage.
